text: CONTRADICTING: Ratiometric OregonGreen-dextran measurement of lumenal pH showed that HsAPOE4-expressing Neuro-2a cells have markedly ALKALINIZED (higher pH, 5.86) endolysosomes compared with HsAPOE3 cells (pH 4.30), i.e. the opposite of the hypothesized APOE4-driven acidification (reported: pH 5.86 (APOE4) vs pH 4.30 (APOE3); ~1.56 pH units higher).
description: Neuro-2a mouse neuroblastoma cells stably carrying the full-length human APOE3 or APOE4 genomic locus (5 kb 5' and 8 kb 3' flanking regions), plus parental HsAPOE-/- control; overnight OregonGreen-488 70,000 MW dextran pulse, 1 h chase, ratiometric 488/458 nm confocal imaging with a 10-point pH-clamp standard curve (pH 3.60-7.50). Caveat: mouse neuronal cell line, not human astrocytes; probe is chased into lysosomes rather than early/recycling endosomes; the hypothesis concerns endosome pH.

provenance.excerpt: We found that HsAPOE4-expressing cells exhibit dramatic lysosomal alkalinization (pH = 5.86) compared to HsAPOE3 (pH = 4.30) cells (Figure 1C-E), reminiscent of previous results in APOE4-expressing astrocyte lysosomes (pH = 5.20, compared to pH = 4.08 in APOE3 astrocytes) [26].

warnings: effect size 'pH 5.86 (APOE4) vs pH 4.30 (APOE3); ~1.56 pH units higher' has no accepted form: recorded as qualitative, numbers kept in description

perturbed.variable: Human APOE4 vs APOE3 genomic locus expressed in Neuro-2a neuronal cells

measured.variable: Absolute lumenal pH of endolysosomes measured by ratiometric OregonGreen-70 kDa dextran with pH-clamp calibration
